The phrase "my compounds are on top of each other" is common informal lab parlance among organic chemists, referring specifically to thin-layer chromatography (TLC) or column chromatography results. When two compounds travel together on a TLC plate or column, their spots or bands overlap and do not separate, meaning they have very similar retention factors (Rf). Retention factor in standard silica gel chromatography is primarily determined by the polarity of the compounds: compounds with similar polarities interact similarly with the stationary phase and elute at the same rate, causing them to "run on top of each other."

The other options do not match this idiomatic expression: similar boiling points cause issues in distillation, similar optical rotations is not a standard separation problem, and non-covalent bonding between compounds would be described as aggregation or sticking together, not traveling "on top of each other" during separation.

Answer: D
